author_connection.full_text: A second grader closed her eyes right in the middle of the story and took a slow deep breath through her nose. Unprompted. She had just learned something she would use for the rest of her life.
author_connection.prohibited_uses: Do not name the school or the child. Do not claim this happens at every reading -- it is one specific, real moment.
author_connection.source_passage: THE CLASSROOM BREATH PRACTICE section, 'the proof moment', verbatim quote.

book_corpus_grounding.note: No structured book-fact registry (volume/chapter/scene/character/location/theme) exists yet in this engine. This field intentionally carries no invented scene, dialogue, or character data -- a human editor must supply book-specific facts directly, grounded in the actual manuscript, before an article can reference specific book content beyond the Author Connection anecdote above.

audience_specific_adjustments.child_reader: Adventure and wonder framing -- the test is 'would this make a kid say I want to go there.'
audience_specific_adjustments.parent_buyer: Educated, nature-oriented, skeptical of screen time and of 'literacy programs' -- speak to what excites their kid about the world, not a curriculum pitch.
audience_specific_adjustments.teacher_librarian: Referral/awareness register, not a sales pitch -- librarians are treated as multipliers, not customers.

brand_voice_profile.emotional_range: Warm sincerity paired with stoic restraint -- affectionate about Charlotte, Henry, and the mission; understated about hardship and struggle.
brand_voice_profile.first_person_style_rules: When Andrew speaks in first person, it must be genuine and specific (a real moment), stoic about hardship (implied, not dramatized), never a manufactured quote.
forbidden_phrases_or_patterns: listicle framing (e.g. '7 Reasons Kids Should Read More')
generic 'reading is important' messaging with no Brave Hearts perspective in it
preachy, lecturing tone -- show, don't lecture
content that any other children's book brand could have posted (no Andrew fingerprint)
brand_voice_profile.humor_rules: Occasional, dry, truthful. Never forced, never at a child's expense, never sarcastic toward the reader.
brand_voice_profile.hype_restrictions: No salesperson energy. No press-release voice. Confidence without hype -- the brand earns trust through specificity, not superlatives.
brand_voice_profile.paragraph_style: Reads like Andrew talking at a farmers market -- conversational, grounded, no corporate structure (no '3 reasons why' framing).
preferred_tone: genuine -- if it sounds like a press release, rewrite it
direct -- say the thing, no padding
warm -- built on love for a real child and a real dog, not a marketing concept
occasionally funny -- direct, dry, truthful humor only, never forced
stoic about hardship -- understated, implied rather than dramatized
recurring_brand_ideas: "I can do hard things" -- the four-word promise behind every book
The breath practice: stop, inhale through the nose, exhale through the mouth
Bravery is not fearlessness -- it's choosing to go anyway
Every challenge in the books is a decision point, not just a plot point
Charlotte is real (Andrew's niece); Henry is real (the dog); the places are real; Andrew's story is real
brand_voice_profile.sentence_style: Short, direct sentences. Say the thing plainly. Avoid throat-clearing lead-ins and padded transitions.
brand_voice_profile.unsupported_outcome_restrictions: Never promise a reading-level jump, a behavior change, or any specific outcome for a specific child. Encouragement, not guarantees.
vocabulary_preferences: concrete, sensory, real-world nouns (real places, real problems: tight boots, fogged goggles, a flat tire)
the brand's own vocabulary: 'the breath', 'decision point', 'brave' (not 'fearless')

global_prohibited_uses: Do not say Andrew went spearfishing 'at Bob Banks' or 'off Bob Banks' -- Bob Banks is a PERSON, a mentor/father figure.
Do not present Nepal as happening before nursing school and NCLEX -- the chronology matters.
Do not reference profit goals or business targets in public-facing content.
Do not describe Andrew as 'just' an author -- he is a nurse, traveler, and founder; the full identity matters.

Do not name a specific Himalayan peak, altitude, or route (e.g. 'Island Peak', 'Jiri to Everest Base Camp') -- the canonical Life Story Skill only confirms 'Himalayan mountaineering' and 'a headwall'; those specific route/peak claims exist only in a supporting blog post and are not corroborated by canonical source.
